T0.scene_summary: A narrow white galley kitchen with a foreground range, opposite countertop and cabinets, a rear doorway, and a potted plant.
T0.overall_evidence: The reconstruction captures the main kitchen arrangement and recognizable stove, cabinetry, doorway and plant. However, the framing and apparent scale differ substantially, and the reference's strong material textures, varied cabinet fronts and directional sunlight are simplified or missing.

main_defects.description: The view is more centered and level, with a much smaller, more cropped stove and a narrower-looking aisle; the reference looks more downward and places the stove prominently across much of the left foreground.
main_defects.evidence: The reference stove extends to the bottom of the image and occupies roughly two fifths of its width, whereas the reconstruction stove is truncated at the left and bottom and occupies roughly one third of the width. The rear doorway also appears smaller and higher in the reconstruction.
main_defects.uncertainty: Differences in camera pose, focal length and object scale may all contribute to the apparent mismatch.

main_defects.description: Prominent surface detail and contrast are greatly reduced: the wood-grain floor, veined marble counter, textured dark stove and distinct cabinet materials become comparatively flat and pale.
main_defects.evidence: The reference has visible wood grain and marble veining, deep green-black stove surfaces and a tan wood drawer, while the reconstruction uses largely uniform surfaces and muted pastel colors.
main_defects.uncertainty: Exposure and lighting differences may also reduce perceived texture and contrast.

main_defects.description: The reference's distinct diagonal patch of direct light and stronger tonal contrast are absent, leaving the reconstruction much more evenly illuminated.
main_defects.evidence: A bright, sharply bounded diagonal shape crosses the floor near the doorway in the reference; no comparable shape appears on the reconstruction floor.
main_defects.uncertainty: The original light source is not visible, and camera or geometry differences could affect the patch's visibility.

main_defects.description: The right-hand cabinetry is reorganized into a more regular array of small drawers rather than the reference's larger white door areas and differently sized dark and wood-colored fronts.
main_defects.evidence: The reference shows a prominent broad white panel, a tan front over a dark front, and a large dark front at the near right; the reconstruction shows repeated smaller fronts with knobs.
main_defects.uncertainty: Perspective and cropping prevent a one-to-one comparison of every cabinet front.

main_defects.description: The plant is shorter and more regularly leafed, lacking the reference's tall sparse silhouette and prominent terminal bud.
main_defects.evidence: The reference plant has a long thin stem topped by a distinct dark bud; the reconstruction has a small, symmetrical series of leaves and no comparable bud.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some apparent size difference may result from camera perspective.

strengths: The narrow galley layout and opposing range and countertop are recognizable.
The rear dark doorway and nearby potted plant are placed in similar relative positions.
The range retains circular cooktop elements, a raised control panel, two purple knobs and a purple oven handle.
White upper cabinets and multicolored lower cabinet fronts are represented.
T0.uncertainty: This is an initial automated visual judgment from two images, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric. Perspective, lighting and cropping can affect apparent proportions and material appearance; hidden geometry was not assessed.

T1.scene_summary: A narrow white kitchen with a stove on the left, a long cabinet and counter on the right, and a doorway and potted plant at the back.
T1.overall_evidence: The major kitchen elements and their left-to-right arrangement are recognizable, including the stove, colored cabinetry, doorway and plant. However, the viewpoint and framing differ substantially, the stove and cabinet fronts have noticeably different apparent proportions and details, and the reconstruction lacks much of the reference's material texture and strong directional lighting.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction looks more straight down the aisle and crops the stove at the left and bottom, whereas the reference shows much more of its front and side and has a more oblique view of the right counter. The doorway also appears narrower and more central in the reconstruction.
main_defects.evidence: The reference stove occupies most of the left foreground with its large dark front visible; in the reconstruction the cooktop is cut off at the left edge and the front is mostly outside the frame. The right countertop recedes differently.
main_defects.uncertainty: Differences in object placement and dimensions may contribute alongside the camera pose and field of view.

main_defects.description: The stove control panel appears much wider and more horizontal relative to the visible range in the reconstruction. The adjoining back-left cabinet is reduced to a thin strip, rather than the substantial turquoise-topped unit visible in the reference.
main_defects.evidence: The reference has a prominent deep turquoise counter behind and to the right of the control panel; the reconstruction shows a narrow pale counter and green vertical face behind the range.
main_defects.uncertainty: Perspective and cropping affect apparent widths, so the underlying object dimensions cannot be determined from the images alone.

main_defects.description: The arrangement and scale of the right-hand cabinet fronts differ: the reference has large white doors and several broad, irregularly grouped colored drawer fronts, while the reconstruction has a denser, more regular grid of smaller fronts.
main_defects.evidence: The large white front in the middle and the large dark near-foreground drawer in the reference are not matched by similarly sized and positioned panels in the reconstruction.
main_defects.uncertainty: The difference in viewpoint and frame crop changes how much of each cabinet is visible.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction is much flatter and more uniformly pale. It omits the pronounced wood grain of the floor, the reference's veined counter surface, and much of the darker metallic and textured contrast on the stove and cabinets.
main_defects.evidence: Reference floorboards have visible grain, the counter has gray streaks, and the range is dark and reflective; reconstruction surfaces are largely smooth and muted.
main_defects.uncertainty: Lighting and image resolution can also reduce apparent texture and contrast.

main_defects.description: The strong diagonal patch of sunlight and its crisp edge on the reference floor are absent; the reconstruction is illuminated much more evenly.
main_defects.evidence: A bright, sharply defined diagonal shape extends from the doorway onto the floor in the reference, but no comparable highlight appears in the reconstruction.
main_defects.uncertainty: The exact source of the reference illumination is not visible.

strengths: The narrow galley-kitchen layout and relative placement of the stove, long right-hand counter, rear doorway and plant are recognizable.
The range has a raised two-knob control panel, circular cooktop elements and a purple-toned handle, echoing the reference.
The right side retains white cabinetry with mixed dark, pale green and light wood-colored fronts, plus upper cabinets.
The rear opening has a similar dark gradient, and the plant is in a low rounded pot to its right.
T1.uncertainty: This is a coarse automated visual judgment from two images, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric. Viewpoint, cropping, lighting and resolution can make geometry and materials look different; occluded or hidden geometry is not assessed.
